I can’t access the web or legal databases right now, so I’m unable to quote the current California statute (as of 2032-01-06) or verify whether your checkout flow complies with it. If you paste the statute text and a precise description or screenshots of your checkout flow (what disclosures appear, exact button/checkbox labels, confirmation email text, and the cancellation mechanism), I can analyze those and point to the specific provisions in the text you provide.

Below are practical next steps and sources where you can verify the statute yourself, plus a short checklist of the common requirements to review against the statute:

Where to get the authoritative statute and guidance
- California Legislative Information (official code text and bill history): https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov
- California Attorney General — consumer protection / automatic renewal guidance: https://oag.ca.gov/consumers
- California codes (search via the Legislative Information site for “automatic renewal” or “automatic renewal law”)

Checklist — items to verify against the statute (confirm each against the official text)
- Pre-purchase disclosures: Does the checkout clearly disclose the automatic renewal/continuous service, the recurring charge amount and frequency, and any material terms before the consumer completes purchase?
- Affirmative consent: Does the flow obtain the consumer’s affirmative consent to the automatic renewal terms (clear checkbox or equivalent, not pre-checked)?
- Acknowledgment/confirmation: Does the merchant provide an acknowledgment copy (e.g., confirmation email) that includes the renewal terms and instructions on how to cancel?
- Cancellation mechanism: Is there a simple, cost-free cancellation method that is at least as easy as the method used to subscribe (and, for online purchases, is online cancellation available)?
- Renewal reminders (if required): If the statute requires renewal reminders prior to charging, are those being sent with the mandated timing and content?
- Recordkeeping & proof: Do you retain proof of the consumer’s consent and the required disclosures?
- Payment and third-party processors: If third-party billing is used, are there additional disclosure/consent requirements?

If you want compliance analysis now:
- Paste the statute text you want me to quote, and paste or describe your checkout flow and any confirmation/cancellation messages exactly. I will quote the provided statute text and analyze whether the flow, as described, matches each provision.

If you prefer, you can consult an attorney for a definitive legal opinion.
